quarterly_data.signal: CFO Charlie Wagner broke cystic fibrosis revenue out by geography. Q2 2026 U.S. CF revenue grew 9% year-over-year, led by strong volume growth from ALYFTREK uptake, continued performance from TRIKAFTA and higher realized net price, while CF revenue outside the U.S. grew 12% year-over-year, driven by strong ALYFTREK launches, timing of orders in certain geographies and the benefit from FX. Global CF revenue growth for the first half of 2026 was 8%, including the benefit of prior year U.S. price increases and foreign exchange, both of which management expects to contribute less to growth in the second half of the year. Q2 2025 results also included $21 million of collaboration revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. CF +9% YoY; ex-U.S. CF +12% YoY; 1H 2026 global CF +8%; Q2 2025 included $21 million of collaboration revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Chief Commercial Officer Duncan McKechnie said ALYFTREK crossed another significant milestone, exceeding $1 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026. In the U.S. patients are initiating ALYFTREK new to therapy, returning to therapy and switching from TRIKAFTA, with the majority of ALYFTREK revenue continuing to come from TRIKAFTA switch patients, and uptake accelerated from the recent approvals in rare mutations as well as patients rolling off open label extension studies. Outside the U.S., with no requirement for augmented liver monitoring in the E.U., more than one in three eligible CF patients in Germany and the U.K. are now benefiting from ALYFTREK.
quarterly_data.figure: ALYFTREK revenue exceeded $1 billion in 1H 2026; majority of revenue from TRIKAFTA switch patients; more than one in three eligible CF patients on ALYFTREK in Germany and the U.K.

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said data presented at ECFS reinforced that ALYFTREK best restores CFTR function amongst the available CFTR modulators: among children with CF under 12 years of age the majority across all eligible genotypes achieve a sweat chloride less than 30 millimoles, nearly 2/3 of younger patients achieved sweat chloride levels less than 30 millimole per liter, and for patients ages 12+ more than 75% achieved sweat chloride levels within the carrier range of CFTR function. She said the unmet need is far lower today and the bar for any medicine to beat ALYFTREK is very, very high, so Vertex will only advance next gen 3.0 assets into phase II and beyond that show promise to beat ALYFTREK with once daily dosing and excellent drug-like properties including drug-drug interactions.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 2/3 of younger patients to sweat chloride less than 30 millimole per liter; more than 75% of patients ages 12+ within the carrier range

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex has initiated global regulatory submissions for ALYFTREK in children ages two to five, and global regulatory submissions for TRIKAFTA in patients ages one to two are also in progress. Duncan McKechnie said the CF growth drivers for the remainder of 2026 are continued ALYFTREK uptake, the label expansion into rare mutations, younger patients and additional geographies.
quarterly_data.figure: ALYFTREK submissions in children ages two to five; TRIKAFTA submissions in patients ages one to two

quarterly_data.signal: Duncan McKechnie said the $76 million of CASGEVY revenue reflected approximately 75% sequential growth versus quarter one 2026 and over 150% year-over-year growth, in line with expectations based on visibility into patient scheduling patterns. There were more CASGEVY infusions in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, and the second quarter was the third sequential quarter with more than 100 patient initiations, which enhances visibility to continued growth for the rest of this year and early 2027 as patients continue to move through cell collection, editing and infusion. Quarter-to-quarter variability in CASGEVY revenue will continue and reflects the timing of patient infusions.
quarterly_data.figure: CASGEVY approximately 75% sequential growth and over 150% year-over-year growth; more infusions in 1H 2026 than in all of 2025; third sequential quarter with more than 100 patient initiations

quarterly_data.signal: New data on CASGEVY at EHA, with simultaneous publication in the New England Journal of Medicine, demonstrated its transformative potential in pediatric patients as well as durable benefits. Last month CASGEVY became the first and only gene therapy FDA approved to treat children as young as two years old in both sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, receiving supplemental approval in the U.S. in a record 53 days post-filing, and the first pediatric patient has already initiated therapy and conducted cell collection. Outside the U.S. CASGEVY regulatory submissions in the five to 11 age group are now complete in Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. supplemental approval in a record 53 days post-filing, down to age two; ex-U.S. submissions for the five to 11 age group complete in Saudi Arabia and the U.K.

quarterly_data.signal: On CASGEVY reimbursement, Duncan McKechnie said Vertex is seeing strong trends in initiations in Germany after reaching a historic reimbursement agreement there, as well as continued strong uptake in the U.K., Italy and the Middle East following the negotiations of sustainable access agreements. He described the CASGEVY story as one of an increasingly robust pipeline of patients initiating the treatment journey.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Duncan McKechnie said JOURNAVX revenue of $50 million reflected sequential revenue growth of approximately 70% and sequential prescription growth of approximately 45% versus quarter one 2026, with revenue positively impacted by channel build after a drawdown in quarter one. Vertex continues to expect some quarterly volatility in inventory build and drawdown as full line wholesalers and retail channel buying patterns normalize to reflect formulary adoption, physician awareness and seasonality in elective surgeries. Rapid prescription growth has also driven greater use of the PSP program than forecast; as physicians and their office staff are educated about quantity limits and prior authorizations Vertex expects the PSP to be triggered less frequently and therefore more revenue to be recognized, and gross to net is now expected to normalize in line with other branded oral medicines in the first half of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: JOURNAVX sequential revenue growth approximately 70% and sequential prescription growth approximately 45%; gross to net to normalize in the first half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Quarter two 2026 JOURNAVX prescriptions totaled approximately 535,000 and just over 900,000 for the first half of 2026, split roughly 50/50 between the hospital and retail channels. In both channels monthly prescriptions were approximately 50,000 in January and doubled to approximately 100,000 in each channel in June. Asked about prescribing behavior, Duncan McKechnie said hospital prescription duration is around about five days, retail is around about 12, 14 days, and it nets out at around about 10 or 11 days for each JOURNAVX prescription, a dynamic that has not changed since launch because it is driven by the dynamics of the institution the patient is in.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 535,000 prescriptions in Q2 and just over 900,000 in 1H 2026; roughly 50/50 hospital and retail; approximately 50,000 per channel per month in January doubling to approximately 100,000 in June; around 10 or 11 days per prescription

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex added approximately 18,000 new HCP prescribers to JOURNAVX in Q2 2026, and JOURNAVX is now on 1,400 hospital and 130 IDN pathways in terms of formulary, protocol or order sets. Duncan McKechnie said prescription growth is ahead of the forecast for 2026, that the breadth and depth of prescriptions across a wide range of settings of care continues to be very strong, and that prescriptions are coming from a broad range of physician types and are being used in a broad range of pain types consistent with the label.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 18,000 new HCP prescribers added in Q2; 1,400 hospital and 130 IDN pathways

quarterly_data.signal: Duncan McKechnie detailed JOURNAVX payer access: a total of 260 million lives covered out of a total possible of approximately 320 million, of which 180 million have unrestricted coverage, leaving 60 million lives yet to be covered and about 80 million lives who have coverage but with some form of restriction such as a 14-day quantity limit or a prior authorization to indication. Vertex recently signed agreements to expand reimbursed access with two additional Medicare Part D plans effective from July 1st, so three of the big four Medicare Part D plans now provide covered access alongside the three large commercial PBMs.
quarterly_data.figure: 260 million covered lives out of approximately 320 million possible; 180 million unrestricted; 60 million yet to be covered; about 80 million restricted; three of the big four Medicare Part D plans plus three large commercial PBMs

quarterly_data.signal: Charlie Wagner said CASGEVY and JOURNAVX combined delivered about $200 million in revenue in the first half of the year, with CASGEVY a bigger contributor than JOURNAVX in that first half, and that Vertex is very confident in getting to its $500 million+ target while declining to give further color on the balance of the year. Duncan McKechnie said Vertex remains on track to exceed its goal of more than tripling the 550,000 JOURNAVX prescriptions and more than tripling revenue from 2025 into 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: CASGEVY plus JOURNAVX about $200 million in 1H 2026; goal to more than triple the 550,000 2025 prescriptions and more than triple revenue in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Reshma Kewalramani said POVI is putting up very strong proteinuria numbers, numerically the best out there: a 52% change from baseline in terms of proteinuria reduction, 70+% reductions in hematuria and 70+% reductions in Gd-IgA1, delivered once monthly in a small volume of 0.46 mils via an auto-injector at home. Duncan McKechnie said approximately 70% of U.S. patients with IgAN have commercial coverage, payer awareness of IgAN and the new BAFF/APRIL inhibitors is high, and Vertex anticipates it will have the largest field force among the novel APRIL or APRIL-BAFF therapies for IgAN. Vertex has also completed the regulatory submission for accelerated approval of POVI in IgAN in Saudi Arabia, where POVI has received breakthrough designation.
quarterly_data.figure: 52% change from baseline in proteinuria, 70+% reductions in hematuria and Gd-IgA1; 0.46 mils once monthly via auto-injector; approximately 70% of U.S. IgAN patients have commercial coverage

quarterly_data.signal: Reshma Kewalramani confirmed that Vertex plans to present the full RAINIER interim analysis data set for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy at a fall conference. She reiterated that the RAINIER phase III interim analysis was a home run, delivering statistically significant and clinically meaningful results across the primary and all secondary endpoints with a favorable safety profile and consistency in the primary endpoint of change from baseline in proteinuria across all groups.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: In primary membranous nephropathy the OLYMPUS phase II/III pivotal trial has completed its phase II portion, the phase III portion initiated last quarter, and the IDMC has completed its review and selected the phase III dose of 80 mg subcutaneously every four weeks; Reshma Kewalramani said the decision was based on the PLA2R biomarker and was not surprising given the RUBY-3 results, where the 80 mg had a very nice reduction in PLA2R. Vertex holds fast track, orphan drug and EMA Prime designations for POVI in membranous. Outside renal, the 30-patient phase II proof of concept study of POVI in myasthenia gravis, evaluating 80 mg and 240 mg doses versus placebo for 12 weeks, is on track to complete enrollment by the end of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: pMN phase III dose of 80 mg subcutaneously every four weeks; gMG 30-patient phase II of 80 mg and 240 mg versus placebo for 12 weeks, enrollment complete by year end

quarterly_data.signal: On AMPLITUDE, the pivotal phase II/III study of inaxaplin in AMKD, Vertex completed enrollment of the interim analysis cohort in September of last year and is on track to complete full enrollment by the end of this year, with the interim analysis conducted following 48 weeks of treatment. Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex has an agreement with the agency for a potential accelerated approval based on the primary endpoint at the time of the interim analysis, which is one-year GFR, in patients with two APOL1 alleles, moderate to heavy proteinuria and depressed GFR, and that a positive result would position Vertex to file for potential accelerated approval in the U.S. thereafter.
quarterly_data.figure: interim analysis conducted following 48 weeks of treatment; accelerated approval agreement based on one-year GFR

quarterly_data.signal: AMPLIFIED, the phase IIB basket study of inaxaplin in expanded AMKD populations not studied in AMPLITUDE - one arm of patients with two APOL1 alleles and diabetes, and one arm with two APOL1 alleles and low-grade proteinuria of 0.2-0.7 g of protein as opposed to 0.7 g and above - has completed enrollment and dosing, with results expected this fall. The AGLOW phase II proof of concept study of VX-407 in ADPKD has completed enrollment and runs with up to 52 weeks of treatment.
quarterly_data.figure: AMPLIFIED low proteinuria arm 0.2-0.7 g versus 0.7 g and above, results this fall; AGLOW with up to 52 weeks of treatment

quarterly_data.signal: Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex had very constructive meetings with the FDA following its voluntary pause to conduct a manufacturing analysis of exemlcel and has resumed dosing patients in the exemlcel phase I/II/III study. With the IND cleared for VX-017, the type O or universal donor cell product, the phase I/II study is expected to initiate in the near term. A silver lining of the pause is that the type O program time differential versus exemlcel has shortened, so Vertex is considering options to further streamline its regulatory strategy and commercialization approach and may bring type O out first or very close behind, with updated T1D plans including timelines expected in the back half of this year. Vertex also continues to progress serial innovation work on improved immunosuppression and hypoimmune programs.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Second quarter 2026 gross margin was 85.6%, an expected sequential step down from Q1 of 2026 that reflects the impact of product mix as well as manufacturing network investments in various products. Charlie Wagner said that as new products, particularly CASGEVY, increase in revenue contribution with higher cost of goods sold than the small molecule CF products, the impact from product mix and manufacturing network investment costs will be more pronounced in the second half than they were in the first half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 gross margin 85.6%

quarterly_data.signal: Second quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.73 represented 5% growth versus the prior year, reflecting strong revenue growth as well as investments in the pipeline and commercial capabilities. The second quarter 2026 non-GAAP effective tax rate was 21.1%, including some one-time expenses, and the year-to-date non-GAAP effective tax rate was 20.4%, within the guidance range of 19.5%-20.5%.
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP EPS $4.73, up 5%; Q2 non-GAAP effective tax rate 21.1%, year-to-date 20.4% against a 19.5%-20.5% range

quarterly_data.signal: During the second quarter Vertex deployed approximately $455 million to repurchase roughly 1 million shares. Charlie Wagner said this activity reflects the ongoing commitment to returning value to shareholders while maintaining the flexibility to act on strategic growth opportunities, and that the top priority for capital deployment remains investing in innovation.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $455 million deployed to repurchase roughly 1 million shares

quarterly_data.signal: The Crinetics acquisition establishes a fifth commercial pillar in specialty endocrine diseases such as acromegaly, CAH and Cushing's syndrome, treated by a concentrated group of specialized endocrinologists that fits directly within the proven efficient specialty commercial model. Duncan McKechnie said Crinetics Q2 results were excellent, with strong growth in paltusotine revenue and patients treated, but held further comment until after the deal closes. The transaction is expected to close in the third quarter and is not yet reflected in guidance; Charlie Wagner said the impact to 2026 revenue and non-GAAP operating expenses should be relatively modest and that updated 2026 guidance will be provided around the time of closing. Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex enters the transaction from a position of strength, viewing CF as a long duration franchise with sustained growth, expecting both CASGEVY and JOURNAVX to be multi-billion dollar assets, and anticipating that the emerging renal franchise could one day rival CF in revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex remains on track to release results later this year from a proof of concept study in DM1. Reshma Kewalramani said the phase II will look at splicing along with the functional endpoints vHOT and QMT, albeit in small numbers of patients, and that she likes the approach because the molecule is an oligo linked to a circular peptide to a nuclear localizing domain peptide, which Vertex believes will allow it to get into the cell and into the nucleus, without the safety tolerability concerns that some other cell-entry mechanisms carry.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: On competition in non-opioid pain, Reshma Kewalramani said that ever since Vertex published VX-150 circa 2017 there has been a spike in others following in its footsteps and pursuing NaV1.8 as a target, that Vertex decided not to advance VX-150 in favor of what is now suzetrigine or VX-548 because of drug-like molecule properties, and that she has never felt better in Vertex history about the possibility of bringing a NaV1.7/1.8 combination to the clinic. On diabetic peripheral neuropathy she said Vertex has been hyper-focused on JOURNAVX in acute pain to get the reimbursement contracts and access done, and will have more to say on DPN, the data and what payers and doctors are looking for in the coming months.
